summary: Deploy the new version first (which applies its Django migration and adds the customer_note column), then backfill existing note values into customer_note so both columns are synchronized, and finally retire the old version.
write_consistency: While both versions are live the old version continues writing to the note column and the new version writes to customer_note. The backfill stage copies all existing note rows into customer_note, after which new writes land in customer_note and old writes stay in note; the two columns remain in sync for the overlap period.
revision_notes: The prior plan executed the backfill stage before deploy_new, so the customer_note column did not yet exist and the UPDATE failed. This revision moves deploy_new first, letting the new version's migration create the column before any data migration runs.

stages.description: Copy existing note values into customer_note so the new version can read them.
sql: UPDATE account_user SET customer_note = note WHERE note IS NOT NULL;

stages.description: Retire the old version after the new version has been running and the note/customer_note values are synchronized.
